discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Feynman's idea of simulating quantum matter with controllable quantum systems became a real laboratory discipline through this work. In 1998 Zoller and collaborators showed that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Bloch and Greiner observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition, establishing atoms in light crystals as clean, programmable analogues of correlated electrons. Greiner's quantum gas microscope (2009) then gave site-resolved, single-atom imaging and control, leading to observations of antiferromagnetic order, entanglement entropy, many-body localization and thermalization in isolated systems. Together these advances created a new experimental paradigm, adopted by laboratories worldwide, that connects condensed-matter physics, quantum information and quantum optics. It is the direct foundation of today's analog and programmable quantum simulators and neutral-atom quantum processors. This is a deep conceptual insight that grew into a broadly used platform for fundamental discovery.
